verdict.rationale: Notes are stored as local plain Markdown files that any script or agent can read/write directly without opening the GUI (obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-2, obsidian-docs-23), and Obsidian Sync even ships a documented headless client explicitly aimed at CI pipelines and agents (obsidian-docs-10). There's also an Obsidian URI protocol for triggering note actions programmatically (obsidian-docs-8) and a plugin Vault API for filesystem interaction (obsidian-gh-1/2), but none of these constitute a first-party, documented REST/vendor API or MCP server purpose-built for AI agent read/write access — that capability is absent from the evidence. Missing for 10: an official vendor REST API or MCP server documented for AI agent read/write access, and independent confirmation that the headless sync client is used this way in practice.
